text: Confirm current threshold logic: DiscountPolicy.discountRate applies a 10% discount when subtotalCents >= 10_000 for non-VIP customers (PricingCalculator applies discountRate to subtotal and rounds).

Follow existing test conventions in /src/test/java/com/sweforge/pricing/PricingCalculatorTest.java (JUnit 5, single instantiated PricingCalculator field, @Test methods using assertEquals against calculator.calculateTotalCents(new Order(List.of(new Item(...))))).
Add a test for subtotal 9,999 cents (e.g., new Item(9_999)) asserting expected total equals 9_999 (no discount, since 9,999 < 10,000).
Add a test for subtotal exactly 10,000 cents (e.g., new Item(10_000)) asserting expected total equals 9_000 (10% discount applies at the boundary, since >= 10,000).
Add a test for subtotal 10,001 cents (e.g., new Item(10_001)) asserting expected total equals the rounded 10% discount, i.e., 9_001 cents (10,001 * 0.9 = 9,000.9, rounds to 9,001).
Use descriptive method names consistent with existing style, e.g. subtotalJustBelowThresholdHasNoDiscount, subtotalAtThresholdGetsBulkDiscount, subtotalJustAboveThresholdGetsBulkDiscount.
Do not modify DiscountPolicy.java, PricingCalculator.java, Order.java, or Item.java -- production code stays unchanged.

Run the relevant tests, e.g. `mvn -Dtest=PricingCalculatorTest test` (or full `mvn test` per pricing-build-validation skill) under Java 21, and confirm all pass including the three new boundary cases.
mvn -Dtest=PricingCalculatorTest test passes with all existing and new tests green
mvn test (full suite) passes with no regressions
Diff shows changes only in the test file (PricingCalculatorTest.java), no edits to src/main/java
New tests explicitly cover subtotals of 9,999, 10,000, and 10,001 cents
